verdict.rationale: uv documents one import path: `uv add -r` pulls every dependency from an existing requirements.txt into the project. Its pip-compatible interface also lets pip and pip-tools projects adopt it without conversion. However, while uv claims to replace poetry, the pack shows no conversion tooling for poetry, pipenv or conda projects or their lockfiles. Community reports of switching from poetry describe outcomes, not import tooling. Missing for 10: documented migration or conversion from poetry, pipenv or conda project files and lockfiles; a dedicated migration guide; independent hands-on corroboration of the requirements.txt import.

support.subject: As a switcher, I can migrate an existing project from the incumbent tool with documented import or conversion tooling

citations.quote: If you're migrating from a `requirements.txt` file, you can use `uv add` with the `-r` flag to add all dependencies from the file
uv provides a drop-in replacement for common `pip`, `pip-tools`, and `virtualenv` commands.
